newsitem.title: USA: GM's Buick grounds Skylark compact car.
newsitem.headline: GM's Buick grounds Skylark compact car.

text.p: General Motors Corp., continuing to thin its overlapping car lineup, said Thursday it will end production of the Buick Skylark compact car by the end of 1997.
The Skylark will vanish from dealer showrooms even sooner -- by the end of the summer, which is the end of the 1997 model year. All 1998 model Skylarks will be sold to fleet buyers, Buick said.

Although the Skylark name has been in and out of Buick's lineup since 1953, it has been used on a number of different types of cars, ranging from a sporty convertible in the 1960s to the current compact sedan and coupe.
"Skylark buyers have more loyalty to the Buick brand than they do to the Skylark," said James Herwaldt, Buick's assistant brand manager for the Skylark.

The decision is part of a major shift by Buick away from smaller cars to allow the division to focus on its revamped mid-size and large car lineup. Buick is now launching its new Century and Regal models and expects Skylark buyers to migrate to the slightly larger Century.
The average transaction price for the Skylark is about $17,700, while the base price for the Century is $18,395, Herwaldt said.
"By the time our dealers sense a shortage of Skylarks, they'll have a pretty full store of Centurys and Regals," Herwaldt said.

Sales of the Skylark have recently improved, rising 39.2 percent to 9,185 for the first two months of 1997, but more than half of the cars are being sold to daily rental fleets -- sales that typically offer little or no profit to GM.
Herwaldt said GM will produce around 15,000 1998 model four-door Skylarks for fleet customers this year at its Lansing, Mich. assembly plant. GM will build no 1998 Skylark coupes.
Buick sold 43,717 Skylarks in the 1996 model year, 48,354 in the 1995 model year, and 61,083 in the 1994 model year.
Starting in 1998, the Lansing plant is scheduled to build a new Pontiac Grand Am model and a new compact car for Oldsmobile, the Alero, which replaces the current Oldsmobile Achieva.
The Skylark name first appeared in 1953 as a limited edition convertible to celebrate Buick's 50th anniversary.

It reappeared in 1962 on a small convertible and coupe and remained in the lineup through the 1972 model year. The name was revived on a 1975 compact car and has been part of the lineup, as a compact, ever since.
